title.zh: 卷六十八 志第二十一 律曆一
title.raw: 卷六十八 志第二十一 律曆一 Volume 68 Treatises 21: Measures and Calendar 1

sentences.zh: 應天 乾元 儀天曆

translations.literal: The Yingtian, Qianyuan, and Yitian calendars.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingtian, Qianyuan, and Yitian Calendars.

sentences.zh: 古者，帝王之治天下，以律曆為先；

translations.literal: In antiquity, when emperors and kings governed All-under-Heaven, they placed pitch pipes and the calendar first.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, rulers placed the regulation of pitch and the calendar foremost in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 儒者之通天人，至律曆而止。

translations.literal: For Confucian scholars who penetrate the connection between Heaven and humanity, their attainment stops at pitch pipes and the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Even for Confucian scholars who sought to unite Heaven and man, the limit of their learning was pitch and calendar.

sentences.zh: 曆以數始，數自律生 ，故律曆既正，寒暑以節，歲功以成，民事以序，庶績以凝，萬事根本由茲立焉。

translations.literal: The calendar begins with number; number arises from pitch — thus once pitch pipes and the calendar are correct, cold and heat are regulated by the seasons, the year's achievement is accomplished, civil affairs are ordered, the manifold accomplishments are consolidated, and the root of the myriad affairs is established hereby.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar begins with number, and number arises from pitch; once pitch and calendar were set right, the seasons kept their rhythm, harvests succeeded, civil life fell into order, and every undertaking gained a foundation.

sentences.zh: 古人 自入小學，知樂知數，已曉其原。

translations.literal: The ancients, from entering the elementary school, knew music and knew number, and already understood its origin.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients learned music and reckoning in elementary school and already grasped these principles at the source.

sentences.zh: 後世老師宿儒猶或弗習律曆，而律曆之家未必知道， 各師其師，岐而二之。

translations.literal: In later ages even veteran teachers and established scholars might still fail to study pitch pipes and the calendar, while specialists in pitch and calendar did not necessarily understand the Way — each honoring his own teacher, they split into two.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages many senior scholars never studied pitch and calendar at all, while specialists in those arts often knew the techniques but not the larger Way — each following his own master until the two fields split apart.

sentences.zh: 雖有巧思，豈能究造化之統會，以識天人之蘊奧哉！

translations.literal: Though there be ingenuity, how could one exhaust the comprehensive unity of creation and transformation, and comprehend the profundity of Heaven and man!
translations.idiomatic: However clever they might be, how could they grasp the full unity of nature or plumb the deep mystery of Heaven and man!

sentences.zh: 是以審律造 曆，更易不常，卒無一定之說。

translations.literal: Therefore in examining pitch and making calendars, changes and replacements were incessant, and in the end there was no fixed theory.
translations.idiomatic: Hence pitch was revised and calendars replaced again and again, until no stable doctrine remained.

sentences.zh: 治效之不古若，亦此之由，而世豈察及是乎！

translations.literal: That governance fell short of antiquity also stems from this — yet did the age ever perceive it!
translations.idiomatic: That government fell short of antiquity owed much to this as well — yet who in the world ever noticed?

sentences.zh: 宋初，承五代之季王朴制律曆、作律準，以宣其聲，太祖以雅樂聲高，詔有司考正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, inheriting the end of the Five Dynasties, Wang Pu made pitch pipes and calendar and made pitch standards to give forth the sounds; Taizu found the court music too high-pitched and ordered the responsible offices to examine and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, inheriting the late Five Dynasties, Wang Pu devised pitch pipes and a calendar and made pitch standards to sound the tones; because Taizu found court music too sharp, he ordered officials to rectify it.

sentences.zh: 和 峴等以影表銅臬暨羊頭秬黍累尺制律，而度量權衡因以取正。

translations.literal: He Yan and others used the shadow table, bronze gnomon, and sheep-head black millet stacked to a foot to make the pitch pipes, and measures, capacity, and weights were thereby set right.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan and his colleagues derived pitch pipes from the shadow table, bronze gnomon, and black millet from Sheep Head Mountain stacked to a foot, and on that basis standardized measures, capacity, and weights.

sentences.zh: 然累代尺度與望臬殊，黍 有鉅細，縱橫容積，諸儒異議，卒無成說。

translations.literal: Yet scales of successive generations differed from the gnomon, millet grains varied in size, and length, breadth, and capacity were disputed — the various scholars disagreed, and in the end no settled view was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scales differed from dynasty to dynasty and from the gnomon standard, millet grains varied in size, and scholars disputed length, breadth, and volume — in the end no consensus was reached.

sentences.zh: 至崇寧中，徽宗任蔡京，信方士「聲為律、 身為度」之說，始大盭乎古矣。

translations.literal: By the Chongning era, Huizong employed Cai Jing and believed the Daoist saying that "sound is pitch, the body is measure," and only then was there a great overturning of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongning period Huizong entrusted Cai Jing, who believed the Daoist doctrine that "sound is pitch and the body is measure," and antiquity was overturned on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 顯德欽天曆亦朴所制也，宋初用之。

translations.literal: The Xiande Qintian calendar was also made by Pu, and was used at the beginning of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiande Qintian calendar was also Wang Pu's work, and the early Song continued to use it.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，以推驗稍疏，詔王處訥等別造新曆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, because verification was somewhat loose, an edict ordered Wang Chunu and others separately to make a new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 (961), because its predictions had grown somewhat loose, the court ordered Wang Chunu and others to compile a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 四 年，曆成，賜名應天，未幾，氣候漸差。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the calendar was completed and given the name Yingtian; before long the seasonal indicators gradually diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later the calendar was finished and named Yingtian; before long its seasonal predictions began to drift.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，行乾元曆，未幾，氣候又差。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo the Qianyuan calendar was adopted; before long the seasonal indicators again diverged.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4 (979) the Qianyuan calendar was adopted; again, before long the seasons fell out of alignment.

sentences.zh: 繼作者曰儀天，曰崇天，曰明天，曰奉元，曰觀天，曰紀元，迨靖康丙午，百六十餘年 ，而八改曆。

translations.literal: Successive works were called Yitian, Chongtian, Mingtian, Fengyuan, Guantian, and Jiyuan — down to Jingkang bingwu, in more than one hundred sixty years, the calendar was changed eight times.
translations.idiomatic: Successors produced the Yitian, Chongtian, Mingtian, Fengyuan, Guantian, and Jiyuan calendars — by Jingkang bingwu (1126), in a little over 160 years, the calendar had been changed eight times.

sentences.zh: 南渡之後，曰統元，曰乾道，曰淳熙，曰會元，曰統天，曰開禧，曰會天 ，曰成天，至德祐丙子，又百五十年，復八改曆。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing came Tongyuan, Qiandao, Chunxi, Huiyuan, Tongtian, Kaixi, Huitian, and Chengtian — down to Deyou bingzi, in another one hundred fifty years, the calendar was again changed eight times.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south came the Tongyuan, Qiandao, Chunxi, Huiyuan, Tongtian, Kaixi, Huitian, and Chengtian calendars — by Deyou bingzi (1296), in another 150 years, eight more revisions had been made.

sentences.zh: 使其初而立法吻合天道，則千歲日至 可坐而致，奚必數數更法，以求幸合玄象哉！

translations.literal: If at the outset the law had matched the Way of Heaven, the winter solstice of a thousand years could have been attained by sitting still — why must one repeatedly change methods to seek a lucky fit with the dark signs!
translations.idiomatic: Had the first laws truly matched Heaven's way, the solstice a millennium hence could have been predicted without rising from one's seat — why revise the methods again and again merely to chase the heavens?!

sentences.zh: 蓋必有任其責者矣。

translations.literal: Surely there must be those who bear the responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Surely someone must bear responsibility for this.

sentences.zh: 雖然，天步惟艱，古今通患，天運日行，左右既分，不能無忒。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, the celestial pace is arduous — a common affliction of antiquity and the present; the heavenly motion runs daily, and once left and right are distinguished, there cannot be without error.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the motion of Heaven is hard to track — a difficulty common to every age; the sky moves day by day, and once east and west are distinguished, some discrepancy is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 謂七十九年差一度，雖 視古差密，亦僅得其概耳。

translations.literal: To say that in seventy-nine years there is a discrepancy of one degree — though tighter than antiquity, one still only grasps the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that precession amounts to one degree in seventy-nine years, though tighter than older estimates, still captures only a rough approximation.

sentences.zh: 又況黃、赤道度有斜正闊狹之殊，日月運行有盈縮、朏朒、 表裡之異。

translations.literal: Moreover, the degrees of the yellow and red equators have differences of obliquity, straightness, breadth, and narrowness; the sun and moon in their motion have variations of surplus and deficit, waxing and waning crescents, and inner and outer aspects.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ecliptic and equatorial degrees differ in obliquity and in apparent breadth, and the sun and moon vary in speed, phase, and apparent position.

sentences.zh: 測北極者，率以千里差三度有奇，晷景稱是。

translations.literal: Those who measure the north pole generally take it that per thousand li there is a difference of somewhat more than three degrees, and the gnomon shadow accords with this.
translations.idiomatic: Observers of the north celestial pole commonly reckon a change of slightly more than three degrees for every thousand li, and gnomon shadows bear this out.

sentences.zh: 古今測驗，止於岳臺，而岳臺 豈必天地之中？

translations.literal: Measurements ancient and modern stop at the Yue Terrace — yet is the Yue Terrace necessarily the center of Heaven and Earth?
translations.idiomatic: All measurements, ancient and modern, were taken at the Yue Terrace — yet was the Yue Terrace truly the center of the world?

sentences.zh: 餘杭則東南，相距二千餘里，華夏幅員東西萬里，發斂晷刻豈能盡諧？

translations.literal: Yuhang lies to the southeast, more than two thousand li distant; the breadth of Huaxia east and west is ten thousand li — how could the moments of solstice and equinox gnomon readings all agree?
translations.idiomatic: Yuhang lies far to the southeast, more than two thousand li away, while China stretches ten thousand li from east to west — how could gnomon readings at every solstice and equinox agree everywhere?

sentences.zh: 又造曆者追求曆元，踰越曠古，抑不知二帝授時齊政之法，畢殫於是否乎？

translations.literal: Again, calendar makers pursue the calendar origin, leaping beyond remote antiquity — yet do they not know whether the method of the Two Emperors in granting the seasons and harmonizing government is wholly exhausted in yes or no?
translations.idiomatic: Calendar makers also chase ever more remote epoch origins — yet have they exhausted the method by which the sage emperors granted the seasons and aligned government with them?

sentences.zh: 是亦儒者所 當討論之大者，諉曰星翁曆生之責可哉？

translations.literal: This too is a great matter that Confucian scholars ought to discuss — can one shrug it off as the responsibility of star masters and calendar clerks?
translations.idiomatic: These are great questions Confucian scholars ought to debate — can they be dismissed as the concern of astrologers and calendar clerks alone?

sentences.zh: 至於儀象推測之具，雖亦數改，若熙寧沈括之 議、宣和璣衡之制，其詳密精緻有出於淳風、令瓚之表者，蓋亦未始乏人也。

translations.literal: As for instruments for observing the sky and making calculations, though they too were changed several times — such as Shen Kuo's proposals in the Xining era and the armillary sphere of the Xuanhe period — in detail, density, and refinement some surpassed Chunfeng and Ling Zan; there have never been lacking such men.
translations.idiomatic: As for observational and computational instruments, though these too were revised repeatedly, Shen Kuo's proposals under Xining and the armillary sphere of the Xuanhe reign were in detail and precision finer than the work of Chunfeng and Ling Zan — the age was never without able men.

sentences.zh: 今其遺法 具在方冊，惟奉元、會天二法不存。

translations.literal: Today their surviving methods are all in the records, except that the Fengyuan and Huitian systems do not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Their surviving methods are preserved in the archives today, except that the Fengyuan and Huitian systems are lost.

sentences.zh: 舊史以乾元、儀天附應天，今亦以乾道、淳熙、會 元附統元，開禧、成天附統天。

translations.literal: The old history appended Qianyuan and Yitian to Yingtian; now Qiandao, Chunxi, and Huiyuan are appended to Tongyuan, and Kaixi and Chengtian to Tongtian.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier history appended Qianyuan and Yitian to Yingtian; here Qiandao, Chunxi, and Huiyuan are appended to Tongyuan, and Kaixi and Chengtian to Tongtian.

sentences.zh: 大抵數異術同，因仍增損，以追合乾象，俱無以大相過 ，備載其法，俾來者有考焉。

translations.literal: In general the numbers differ but the methods are the same — inheriting and adding or subtracting to pursue conformity with the celestial signs — none greatly surpasses the others; their methods are fully recorded so that those to come may have material for examination.
translations.idiomatic: In general the figures differ but the methods are the same, each revision inheriting and adjusting the last to chase the heavens — none stands far above the rest; all are recorded here so that posterity may study them.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝作律呂，以調陰陽之聲，以候天地之氣。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor made the pitch pipes to regulate the sounds of yin and yang and to observe the qi of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor devised the pitch pipes to harmonize yin and yang in sound and to read the breath of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 堯則欽若曆象，以授人時，以成歲功， 用能綜三才之道，極萬物之情，以成其政化者也。

translations.literal: Yao then reverently conformed to the calendar and celestial signs, to grant the people's seasons and accomplish the year's work — thereby able to comprehend the Way of the three powers and exhaust the sentiments of the myriad things, and accomplish his government and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yao reverently aligned the calendar and the heavens to grant the seasons to the people and complete the year's work, thereby mastering the way of Heaven, earth, and man and bringing all things into his civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 至司馬遷、班固敘其指要，著之簡策 。

translations.literal: When Sima Qian and Ban Gu narrated their essential points, they set them down on bamboo slips.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian and Ban Gu later summarized these principles and committed them to writing.

sentences.zh: 自漢至隋，歷代祖述，益加詳悉。

translations.literal: From Han to Sui, successive generations followed and transmitted, adding ever greater detail.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Sui each dynasty followed and elaborated the tradition with growing detail.

sentences.zh: 暨唐貞觀迄周顯德，五代隆替，踰三百年，博達之 士頗亦詳緝廢墜，而律志皆闕。

translations.literal: From Tang Zhenguan down to Zhou Xiande, through the rise and fall of the Five Dynasties for more than three hundred years, learned men also compiled in detail what had fallen into ruin — yet the treatises on pitch were all missing.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang Zhenguan to Later Zhou Xiande, through more than three centuries of the Five Dynasties, learned men did much to recover what had been lost — yet treatises on pitch were absent from the histories.

sentences.zh: 宋初混一○內，能士畢舉，國經王制，悉復古道。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, unifying within the four seas, able men were all raised up, and state constants and royal institutions all restored the ancient Way.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song unified the realm, able men were appointed everywhere, and state institutions were restored to the ancient pattern.

sentences.zh: 漢志 有備數、和聲、審度、嘉量、權衡之目，後代因之，今亦用次序以志於篇：

translations.literal: The Han Treatise has the categories of providing number, harmonizing sound, examining measure, excellent capacity, and weights and balances; later generations followed it — now we also use this order to record them in the chapter:
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise listed providing number, harmonizing sound, examining measure, standard capacity, and weights and balances; later histories followed that order, and this chapter does the same:

sentences.zh: 曰備數。

translations.literal: It is called Providing Number.
translations.idiomatic: Providing Number.

sentences.zh: 周禮，保氏教國子以六藝，其六曰九數，謂方田、粟米、差分、少廣、商功、 均輸、方程、贏朒、旁要，是為九章。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Guardian taught the sons of the state the Six Arts; the sixth is the Nine Numbers — namely field measurement, millet and rice, proportional distribution, lesser breadth, engineering works, fair levies, simultaneous equations, surplus and deficit, and right triangles — these are the Nine Chapters.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou records that the Guardian taught the crown princes six arts, the sixth being the nine branches of reckoning: field measurement, grain, proportional parts, lesser width, engineering, fair transport, simultaneous equations, excess and deficit, and right triangles — the Nine Chapters.

sentences.zh: 其後又有海島、孫子、五曹、張丘建、夏侯陽、 周髀、綴術、緝古等法相因而起，歷代傳習，謂之小學。

translations.literal: Afterward there also arose in succession methods such as Sea Island, Master Sun, Five Officials, Zhang Qiujian, Xiahou Yang, Zhou Bi, Continuation of Methods, and Restoration of Antiquity — transmitted and studied through the generations, called elementary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Later came the Sea Island, Master Sun, Five Officials, Zhang Qiujian, Xiahou Yang, Zhou Bi, Continuation of Methods, and Restoration of Antiquity texts, handed down through the ages as elementary mathematics.

sentences.zh: 唐試右千牛衛胄曹參軍陳從運 著得一算經，其術以因折而成，取損益之道，且變而通之，皆合於數。

translations.literal: In Tang, the probationary Right Thousand-Ox Guard Arsenal Clerk Chen Congyun authored the Yide Suanjing; its methods are accomplished by folding and inheriting, taking the way of decrease and increase, and moreover changing and extending them — all conforming to number.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, Chen Congyun, probationary clerk of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, wrote the Canon of Unified Calculation, whose methods build by successive adjustment through increase and decrease until all accord with number.

sentences.zh: 復有徐仁美者， 作增成玄一法，設九十三問，以立新術，大則測於天地，細則極於微妙，雖粗述其事， 亦適用於時。

translations.literal: There was also Xu Renmei, who made the method of augmented formation and dark unity, setting forth ninety-three problems to establish new methods — great ones measuring Heaven and Earth, fine ones reaching to subtlety; though roughly narrating the matter, it was also applicable to the time.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Renmei also devised the method of augmented formation and dark unity with ninety-three problems establishing new techniques — ranging from measurements of heaven and earth down to the most subtle quantities; though only roughly described, it served the needs of the age.

sentences.zh: 古者命官屬於太史，漢、魏之世，皆在史官。

translations.literal: In antiquity offices were appointed subordinate to the Grand Astrologer; in Han and Wei times they were all under the historiographical offices.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity these offices belonged to the Grand Astrologer; under Han and Wei they remained with the historiographical staff.

sentences.zh: 隋氏始置算學博士於國庠， 唐增其員，宋因而不改。

translations.literal: The Sui first established Doctors of Computational Learning at the National University; Tang increased their number, and Song followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui first appointed Doctors of Computational Learning at the National University; Tang increased their number, and Song left the arrangement unchanged.

sentences.zh: 曰和聲。

translations.literal: It is called Harmonizing Sound.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing Sound.

sentences.zh: 周禮，典同掌六律六同之和，凡為樂器，以十有二律為之數度。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Director of Harmonies oversees the harmony of the six pitch standards and six unisons; in making musical instruments, the twelve pitch pipes provide their numerical measures.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou assigns the Director of Harmonies to regulate the six pitch standards and six unisons; all instruments take their dimensions from the twelve pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 古之聖人推律 以製器，因器以宣聲，和聲以成音，比音而為樂。

translations.literal: The sages of antiquity derived pitch to make instruments, used instruments to give forth sound, harmonized sounds to form notes, and compared notes to make music.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sages derived pitch to fashion instruments, used instruments to produce sound, harmonized sounds into tones, and combined tones into music.

sentences.zh: 然則律呂之用，其樂之本歟！

translations.literal: Thus the use of pitch pipes — are they not the root of music!
translations.idiomatic: Thus pitch pipes are the very foundation of music!

sentences.zh: 以其相 生損益，數極精微，非聰明博達，則罕能詳究。

translations.literal: Because their mutual generation and decrease and increase reach the utmost refinement in number, unless one is intelligent and broadly accomplished, few can investigate them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Because their cycles of generation and diminution involve numbers of the utmost refinement, only the most penetrating minds could master them fully.

sentences.zh: 故歷代而下，其法或存或闕，前史言之 備矣。

translations.literal: Therefore down through the generations their methods were sometimes preserved and sometimes lost — the former histories speak of this fully.
translations.idiomatic: Down the generations the methods were sometimes preserved and sometimes lost — earlier histories record this at length.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，王樸始依周法，以秬黍校正尺度，長九寸，虛徑三分，為黃鐘之管， 作律準，以宣其聲。

translations.literal: In Zhou Xiande, Wang Pu first followed Zhou methods, using black millet to correct the scale — nine inches long, hollow diameter three fen — as the yellow bell pipe, and made pitch standards to give forth its sound.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Zhou Xiande, Wang Pu first followed Zhou methods, using black millet to set the scale: a nine-inch pipe with a hollow diameter of three fen for the yellow bell, and pitch standards to sound it.

sentences.zh: 宋乾德中，太祖以雅樂聲高，詔有司重加考正。

translations.literal: In Song Qiande, Taizu found the court music too high and ordered the responsible offices to examine and correct it anew.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Qiande (963–968), Taizu found court music too sharp and ordered officials to re-examine it.

sentences.zh: 時判太常寺和峴上 言曰：「古聖設法，先立尺寸，作為律呂，三分損益，上下相生，取合真音，謂之形器 。

translations.literal: At that time the acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, He Yan, memorialized: "The ancient sages established methods by first setting dimensions, making them into pitch pipes — decrease and increase by thirds, generating upward and downward, taking conformity with true sound — this is called the formed instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, He Yan, memorialized: "The ancient sages first established dimensions and from them derived the pitch pipes, diminishing and augmenting by thirds to generate the scale until true pitch was reached — these are the physical instruments.

sentences.zh: 但以尺寸長短非書可傳，故累秬黍求為準的，後代試之，或不符會。

translations.literal: But because the length and shortness of dimensions cannot be transmitted in writing, therefore black millet was stacked to seek a standard — later generations tested it, and sometimes it did not accord.
translations.idiomatic: Because exact lengths cannot be conveyed in writing, black millet was stacked to provide a standard, yet later trials often failed to match.

sentences.zh: 西京銅望臬可校 古法，即今司天臺影表銅臬下石尺是也。

translations.literal: The bronze gnomon of the Western Capital can correct the ancient method — that is today's stone foot beneath the bronze gnomon of the shadow table at the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The bronze gnomon of the Western Capital can verify the ancient standard — the stone foot beneath the shadow table at the Directorate of Astronomy today.

sentences.zh: 及以樸所定尺比校，短於石尺四分，則聲樂之 高，蓋由於此。

translations.literal: When the foot that Pu had fixed was compared, it was four fen shorter than the stone foot — the height of the musical sounds surely stemmed from this.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's foot proved four fen shorter than the stone foot — which explains why the music sounded too high.

sentences.zh: 況影表測於天地，則管律可以準繩。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the shadow table is measured against Heaven and Earth — then the pitch pipes can serve as the plumb line."
translations.idiomatic: Since the shadow table is measured against heaven and earth, the pitch pipes can be set by that standard."

sentences.zh: 上乃令依古法，以造新尺并黃鐘 九寸之管，命工人校其聲，果下於樸所定管一律。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered that according to the ancient method a new foot and a yellow bell pipe of nine inches be made; workers were ordered to test the sound — it indeed fell one pitch standard below the pipe Pu had fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered a new foot and a nine-inch yellow bell pipe made by the ancient method; when craftsmen tested the sound, it proved a full pitch lower than Pu's pipe.

sentences.zh: 又內出上黨羊頭山秬黍，累尺校律， 亦相符合。

translations.literal: The palace also produced black millet from Sheep Head Mountain in Shangdang; stacked to a foot to test the pitch pipes, it also accorded.
translations.idiomatic: The palace also supplied black millet from Sheep Head Mountain in Shangdang; stacked to a foot, it matched the pitch pipes as well.

sentences.zh: 遂下尚書省集官詳定，眾議僉同。

translations.literal: An order was then sent down to the Department of State Affairs to assemble officials for detailed determination; the assembled discussion was unanimous.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Department of State Affairs for a joint review, and all officials agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是重造十二律管，自此雅音和暢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the twelve pitch pipes were remade, and from this the court music was harmonious and smooth.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve pitch pipes were then remade, and from that time court music sounded in proper harmony.

sentences.zh: 曰審度者，本起於黃鐘之律，以秬黍中者度之，九十黍為黃鐘之長，而分、寸、尺、丈 、引之制生焉。

translations.literal: It is called Examining Measure: it originally arises from the pitch standard of the yellow bell; the medium black millet grain measures it — ninety grains are the length of the yellow bell, and the systems of fen, cun, chi, zhang, and yin are thereby produced.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Measure: the standard derives from the yellow bell pitch pipe; the medium grain of black millet defines it — ninety grains equal the length of the yellow bell, from which the units of fen, inch, foot, rod, and cord are derived.

sentences.zh: 宋既平定四方，凡新邦悉頒度量於其境，其偽俗尺度踰於法制者去之。

translations.literal: Once Song had pacified the four quarters, every new domain was entirely issued measures within its borders; false popular scales that exceeded the legal system were removed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song pacified the realm, every newly subdued territory received official measures, and local scales that exceeded the legal standard were abolished.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，又禁民間造者。

translations.literal: In Qiande, private manufacture was again forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande private manufacture was also banned.

sentences.zh: 由是尺度之制盡復古焉。

translations.literal: Thereby the system of linear measure was wholly restored to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the system of linear measure was fully restored to the ancient standard.

sentences.zh: 曰嘉量。

translations.literal: It is called Excellent Capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent Capacity.

sentences.zh: 周禮，○氏為量。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Granary Master makes the measures.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou assigns the Granary Master to make the measures.

sentences.zh: 漢志云，物有多少受以量，本起於黃鐘之管容秬黍千二百， 而龠、合、升、斗、斛五量之法備矣。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise says: things have more or less and are received by measure; it originally arises from the yellow bell pipe holding twelve hundred black millet grains — and the methods of the five capacities yue, ge, sheng, dou, and hu are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise states that things vary in amount and are measured accordingly; the standard began with the yellow bell pipe holding twelve hundred grains of black millet, establishing the five capacities from yue through hu.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，詔有司精考古式，作為嘉量，以頒天 下。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the abdication, he ordered the responsible offices to examine ancient models with care and make excellent capacity measures to distribute throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu received the abdication, he ordered officials to study ancient models carefully and cast standard capacity measures to distribute throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其後定西蜀，平嶺南，復江表，泉、浙納土，并、汾歸命，凡四方斗、斛不中式者 皆去之。

translations.literal: Afterward Western Shu was settled, Lingnan pacified, the lands south of the Yangzi recovered, Quan and Zhe submitted, Bing and Fen surrendered — wherever dou and hu in the four quarters did not conform to the standard, they were all removed.
translations.idiomatic: After Western Shu was subdued, Lingnan pacified, the lower Yangzi recovered, Quanzhou and Zhejiang submitted, and Bing and Fen surrendered, every nonstandard bushel and picul in the realm was abolished.

sentences.zh: 嘉量之器，悉復昇平之制焉。

translations.literal: The vessels of excellent capacity all restored the Shengping system.
translations.idiomatic: The standard capacity measures were thus restored to the unified system of the age.

sentences.zh: 曰權衡之用，所以平物一民、知輕重也。

translations.literal: The use of weights and balances is to equalize things and unify the people, and to know light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Weights and balances serve to standardize goods, unite the people, and distinguish heavy from light.

sentences.zh: 權有五，曰銖、兩、斤、鈞、石，前史言之詳 矣。

translations.literal: There are five weights: zhu, liang, jin, jun, and shi — the former histories speak of them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: There are five weight units — zhu, liang, jin, jun, and shi — which earlier histories describe in full.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年八月，詔有司按前代舊式作新權衡，以頒天下，禁私造者。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Jianlong, an edict ordered the responsible offices to follow the old models of former dynasties and make new weights and balances to distribute throughout the realm, forbidding private manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jianlong 1 (960), officials were ordered to follow former dynasties' models in casting new weights and balances for distribution throughout the realm and to forbid private manufacture.

sentences.zh: 及平荊湖，即 頒量、衡於其境。

translations.literal: When Jing and Hu were pacified, measures and balances were immediately distributed within their borders.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinghu was pacified, the new measures and weights were immediately distributed there.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年三月三日，詔曰：「書云：『協時、月，正日，同律、度、 量、衡。』

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month of the third year of Chunhua, an edict said: "The Book says: 'Harmonize the seasons and months, rectify the days, and unify pitch, measure, capacity, and balance.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the third month of Chunhua 3 (992), an edict cited the Book: "Harmonize the seasons and months, rectify the days, and unify pitch, measure, capacity, and balance.

sentences.zh: 所以建國經而立民極也。

translations.literal: This is how to establish the state's warp and set up the people's pole.
translations.idiomatic: This is how a state establishes its foundations and sets the standard for the people.

sentences.zh: 國家萬邦咸乂，九賦是均，顧出納於有司，繫權衡 之定式。

translations.literal: The state: the myriad domains are all governed, the nine levies are equalized — yet receipts and disbursements rest with the responsible offices, tied to the fixed patterns of weights and balances.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm is at peace and taxes are fairly levied, all receipts and disbursements depend on officials and ultimately on fixed weights and balances.

sentences.zh: 如聞秬黍之制，或差毫釐，錘鈞為姦，害及黎庶。

translations.literal: We have heard that in the standard of black millet there may be discrepancies of a hair or a li — hammers and steelyards become instruments of fraud, harming the common people.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that even the black-millet standard may err by a hair or a fraction, allowing fraud with steelyards and scales that harms the common people.

sentences.zh: 宜令詳定稱法，著為通規。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to order a detailed fixing of weighing methods and set them forth as a general regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Let weighing methods be examined in detail and established as a general regulation."

sentences.zh: 事下有司，監內藏庫、崇儀使劉承珪言：「太府寺舊銅式自一錢至十斤，凡五十一， 輕重無準。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the responsible offices; Liu Chenggui, commissioner of the Inner Storehouse and palace ritual envoy, said: "The old bronze standards of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, from one cash to ten jin — fifty-one in all — had no fixed light or heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the responsible offices; Liu Chenggui, commissioner of the Inner Storehouse, reported: "The Court of the Imperial Treasury's old bronze standards, from one cash to ten jin — fifty-one in all — had no consistent weight.

sentences.zh: 外府歲受黃金，必自毫釐計之，式自錢始，則傷於重。」

translations.literal: The outer treasuries yearly receive gold and must reckon from the smallest units; if the standard begins from cash, it is injurious in heaviness."
translations.idiomatic: The outer treasuries receive gold yearly and must reckon to the finest fraction; standards beginning at one cash are too coarse."

sentences.zh: 遂尋究本末，別製 法物。

translations.literal: He then traced root and branch and separately made legal objects.
translations.idiomatic: He then traced the matter to its roots and cast new standard weights.

sentences.zh: 至景德中，承珪重加參定，而權衡之制益為精備。

translations.literal: By the Jingde era Chenggui again added examination and fixing, and the system of weights and balances became ever more refined and complete.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jingde era Chenggui revised them again, and the system of weights and balances became still more precise.

sentences.zh: 其法蓋取漢志子穀秬黍為則， 廣十黍以為寸，從其大樂之尺，

translations.idiomatic: The musical foot is derived from the yellow bell pipe.

translations.idiomatic: (The two methods derive li and lei from the foot and millet.)

translations.literal: and by the measure-foot sought li,
translations.idiomatic: And by the measure-foot derived li,

translations.idiomatic: (Measure is the general term for rod and foot.

translations.idiomatic: From accumulated millet grains, one derives lei.

translations.literal: (From accumulated millet and taking lei, then ten millet make one lei, ten lei one zhu, twenty-four zhu one liang.
translations.idiomatic: (Deriving lei from accumulated millet: ten grains make one lei, ten lei one zhu, and twenty-four zhu one liang.

translations.idiomatic: All weight pieces are cast in copper.)

translations.literal: Using li and lei, made two scales equal to one qian-half and one liang, each suspending three hao, to align them by stars.
translations.idiomatic: Using li and lei, he made two scales calibrated at one and a half qian and one liang, each fitted with three hao markers aligned by star graduations.

sentences.zh: 等一錢半者，以取一稱之法。

translations.literal: The one equal to one qian-half served to obtain the method of one scale.
translations.idiomatic: The scale set at one and a half qian provided the standard for a single-balance method.

sentences.zh: 其衡合樂尺一尺二寸，重一錢，錘重六分，盤重五分。

translations.literal: Its beam matched the music foot at one chi two cun, weighed one qian, the weight six fen, the pan five fen.
translations.idiomatic: Its beam measured one chi two cun on the musical foot; it weighed one qian, with a six-fen weight and a five-fen pan.

sentences.zh: 初毫星準半錢，至稍總一錢半， 析成十五分，分列十氂；

translations.literal: The first hao star-aligned at half qian, to the tip totaling one qian-half, divided into fifteen fen, arrayed in ten li;
translations.idiomatic: From the first hao marker, star-aligned at half a qian, to the tip totaling one and a half qian, it was divided into fifteen fen, each subdivided into ten li;

sentences.zh: 〈（第一毫下等半錢，當五十氂，若十五斤稱等五斤也。）〉

translations.literal: (The first hao below equal to half qian, equivalent to fifty li, as on a fifteen-jin scale the five-jin mark.)
translations.idiomatic: (The first hao below equals half a qian, or fifty li—like the five-jin mark on a fifteen-jin steelyard.)

sentences.zh: 中毫 至稍一錢，析成十分，分列十氂；

translations.literal: Middle hao to tip one qian, divided into ten fen, arrayed in ten li;
translations.idiomatic: From the middle hao to the tip at one qian, it was divided into ten fen, each into ten li;

sentences.zh: 末毫至稍半錢，析成五分，分列十氂。

translations.literal: Last hao to tip half qian, divided into five fen, arrayed in ten li.
translations.idiomatic: From the last hao to the tip at half a qian, it was divided into five fen, each into ten li.

sentences.zh: 等一兩者，亦 為一稱之則。

translations.literal: The one equal to one liang also served as the standard of one scale.
translations.idiomatic: The scale set at one liang likewise served as the standard for a single balance.

sentences.zh: 其衡合樂分尺一尺四寸，重一錢半，錘重六錢，盤重四錢。

translations.literal: Its beam matched the music fen-foot at one chi four cun, weighed one qian-half, weight six qian, pan four qian.
translations.idiomatic: Its beam measured one chi four cun on the musical fractional foot; it weighed one and a half qian, with a six-qian weight and a four-qian pan.

sentences.zh: 初毫至稍，布 二十四銖，下別出一星，等五絫；

translations.literal: First hao to tip, laid out twenty-four zhu, below each set out one star, equal to five lei;
translations.idiomatic: From the first hao to the tip, twenty-four zhu were laid out; below each, an extra star mark equaled five lei;

sentences.zh: 〈（每銖之下，復出一星，等五絫，則四十八星等二百 四十絫，計二千四百絫為十兩。）〉

translations.literal: (Below each zhu again one star, equal to five lei, then forty-eight stars equal two hundred forty lei, reckoning two thousand four hundred lei for ten liang.)
translations.idiomatic: (Below each zhu another star equals five lei; forty-eight stars thus equal two hundred forty lei, and two thousand four hundred lei total ten liang.)

sentences.zh: 中毫至稍五錢，布十二銖，列五星，星等二絫；

translations.literal: Middle hao to tip five qian, laid twelve zhu, arrayed five stars, each star equal two lei;
translations.idiomatic: From the middle hao to the tip at five qian, twelve zhu were laid out with five stars, each star equaling two lei;

sentences.zh: 〈（布 十二銖為五錢之數，則一銖等十絫，都等一百二十絫為半兩。）〉

translations.literal: (Laying twelve zhu for the number of five qian, then one zhu equals ten lei, all equal one hundred twenty lei for half liang.)
translations.idiomatic: (Twelve zhu laid out for five qian means one zhu equals ten lei, or one hundred twenty lei for half a liang.)

sentences.zh: 末毫至稍六銖，銖列十 星，星等絫。

translations.literal: Last hao to tip six zhu, each zhu arrayed ten stars, each star equal lei.
translations.idiomatic: From the last hao to the tip at six zhu, each zhu bore ten stars, each star equaling one lei.

sentences.zh: 〈（每星等一絫，都等六十絫為二錢半。）〉

translations.literal: (Each star equal one lei, all equal sixty lei for two qian-half.)
translations.idiomatic: (Each star equals one lei; sixty lei in all make two and a half qian.)

sentences.zh: 以御書真、草、行三體淳化錢， 較定實重二銖四絫為一錢者，以二千四百得十有五斤為一稱之則。

translations.literal: Using Imperial-script regular, cursive, and running-script Chunhua coins, compared and fixed the actual weight at two zhu four lei for one qian, using two thousand four hundred obtaining fifteen jin as the standard of one scale.
translations.idiomatic: Calibrating against Chunhua coins in regular, cursive, and running imperial scripts, he fixed the true weight at two zhu four lei per qian; two thousand four hundred grains thus yielded fifteen jin as the standard for the larger scale.

sentences.zh: 其法，初以積黍為準 ，然後以分而推忽，為定數之端。

translations.literal: Its method, first taking accumulated millet as standard, then by fen deducing hu, as the starting point of fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The method began with accumulated millet as the standard, then derived hu through fen as the foundation of fixed quantities.

sentences.zh: 故自忽、絲、毫、氂、黍、絫、銖各定一錢之則。

translations.literal: Therefore from hu, si, hao, li, millet, lei, zhu each fixed a one-qian standard.
translations.idiomatic: Thus hu, si, hao, li, millet, lei, and zhu each received a fixed standard at one qian.

sentences.zh: 〈（ 謂皆定一錢之則，然後制取等稱也。）〉

translations.idiomatic: (That is, each unit was fixed at one qian before the graduated scales were manufactured.)

translations.idiomatic: (One thousand si make one fen; ten thousand si define one qian.)

translations.idiomatic: (One hundred hao make one fen; one thousand hao define one qian.

translations.idiomatic: Ten li make one fen;

translations.literal: (Ten li for one fen, using one hundred li fixed as the standard of one qian.
translations.idiomatic: (Ten li make one fen; one hundred li define one qian.

translations.idiomatic: Each unit increases tenfold until one qian is reached.

translations.idiomatic: (The tenfold progression fixes standards from ten thousand hu up to one hundred thousand hu.)

translations.idiomatic: Millet uses two thousand four hundred grains per liang;

sentences.zh: 又儀天有求次正定日加 時黃道日度，置歲差，以限數乘之，退一位，滿一百一為差秒及小分，再析之，乃以加 一象度，所得，累加冬至黃道日，滿黃道宿次去之，各得四正，即加時黃道日度也。

translations.literal: Yitian also has a method to find the hour-added ecliptic solar degree on the next fixed upright day: place the annual difference, multiply by the limit number, retreat one place, full 101 yields difference seconds and minor parts, subdivide again, then add one image degree; accumulate from the winter solstice ecliptic day, remove full ecliptic lodges — thereby obtaining each of the four uprights, which are the hour-added ecliptic solar degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Yitian also gives the hour-added ecliptic degree on each fixed upright day: take the annual precession, multiply by the limit number, reduce one place, and divide by 101 for seconds and minor parts; subdivide again, add one image degree, accumulate from the winter solstice ecliptic position, and drop full lodges — obtaining the four uprights as hour-added ecliptic degrees.

sentences.zh: 若 求四正定日夜半黃道日度，置其定日小餘副之，以其日盈縮分乘之，滿宗法而一，盈加 縮減其副，乃以減其日加時，即為夜半黃道日度。

translations.literal: To find the midnight ecliptic solar degree on the four upright fixed days: set aside the fixed day's minor remainder as auxiliary, multiply by that day's excess-deficit parts, divide by the lineage factor when full, add for excess or subtract for deficit from the auxiliary, then subtract from the day's hour-added value — this is the midnight ecliptic solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: For midnight ecliptic degrees on the four upright days: take the fixed day's minor remainder as auxiliary, multiply by that day's excess-deficit, divide by the lineage factor, adjust the auxiliary for excess or deficit, subtract from the hour-added degree — yielding the midnight ecliptic position.

sentences.zh: 又有求每日夜半日度，因四正初日夜 半度，累加一策，以其日盈縮分盈加縮減，滿黃道宿次去之，即得每日夜半日度。

translations.literal: There is also finding the midnight solar degree for each day: starting from the midnight degree on the first night of each upright, accumulate one interval, apply that day's excess-deficit parts adding for excess and subtracting for deficit, remove full ecliptic lodges — thereby obtaining each day's midnight solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: To find each day's midnight solar degree: begin from the midnight degree at the first night of each upright, add one day's interval, adjust by that day's excess-deficit, and drop full ecliptic lodges.

sentences.zh: 又有 求定朔、弦、望加時日度，置定朔、望小餘副之，以其日盈縮分乘之，以宗法收之為分 ，盈加縮減其副，以加其日夜半度，各得其時加日躔所次。

translations.literal: There is also finding the hour-added solar degree at fixed new moon, quarter, and full moon: set aside the fixed new- or full-moon minor remainder as auxiliary, multiply by that day's excess-deficit parts, collect by the lineage factor into parts, add for excess or subtract for deficit from the auxiliary, add to that day's midnight degree — thereby obtaining where the hour-added solar motion stands.
translations.idiomatic: There is also the hour-added solar degree at fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon: use the fixed minor remainder as auxiliary, multiply by the day's excess-deficit, reduce by the lineage factor, adjust the auxiliary, add to the midnight degree — locating the sun at the desired hour.
